findings.highlight: This was never an opponent we could beat unscathed.
findings.evidenceJa: 捨て身でなくては敵わぬ相手だ
findings.governingReading: Saber accepts that defeating Gilgamesh requires 捨て身—throwing her life/body away in the attempt.
findings.explanation: An enemy requiring a self-sacrificial attack becomes one that cannot be beaten unscathed.

findings.highlight: Saber breathes in deeply and considers her condition.
findings.evidenceJa: 深く吸い込んだ息を吐いて、体調を整える。
findings.governingReading: With one minute remaining, she exhales the deep breath she drew and adjusts her bodily condition.
findings.explanation: Saber's measured exhalation and physical preparation become inhaling and considering her condition.

findings.highlight: Her voice lacks its usual grace.
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーの声に色はない。
findings.governingReading: Shock strips emotional color from her voice when she recognizes Assassin.
findings.explanation: Saber's colorless voice becomes a voice lacking grace.

findings.highlight: A Servant cannot maintain themselves without a physical body, even if one is a mage.
findings.evidenceJa: いかに魔術師と言えど、実体を持たぬサーヴァントにサーヴァントは維持できぬ。
findings.governingReading: Even a magus cannot sustain a Servant when that magus is herself a non-corporeal Servant; the anchor must belong to the current era, so Caster selected the gate.
findings.explanation: Caster's inability as a bodiless Servant to anchor another Servant becomes Assassin needing a physical body.

findings.highlight: Unless she hurries, her allies will arrive while she's fighting Gilgamesh.
findings.evidenceJa: 急がなければ、ふたりはギルガメッシュとの戦いに間に合ってしまう。
findings.governingReading: Saber must hurry because otherwise the pair will catch up to the Gilgamesh battle; in the worst case they confront him before she even reaches the precincts.
findings.explanation: Rin and Shirou arriving in time to confront Gilgamesh becomes arriving while Saber is already fighting him.

findings.highlight: I wasn't wealthy enough to have a name of my own.
findings.evidenceJa: 名前を持つほど余裕のある人間ではなかった
findings.governingReading: The nameless swordsman says he could not read or write and was not the sort of person with the余裕—means, latitude, or life circumstances—to have a name.
findings.explanation: Having no social latitude to possess a name becomes not being wealthy enough to have one.

findings.highlight: superior swordsman, something he was never allowed to witness in life.
findings.evidenceJa: 上等すぎる剣士との対決を、死の際でさえ夢見た
findings.governingReading: Assassin imagines that, even at death, his unnamed self may have dreamed of crossing swords with a swordsman too exalted for him to face.
findings.explanation: A nameless swordsman being forbidden a duel with a superior becomes being unable to witness one.
